Check: 'savoury meat' is 'tasty food'; 'venison' is 'wild meat'; 'firstborn' is 'oldest son'; verse 29 'be lord over thy brethren' is 'be the master of your brothers'; verse 40 'break his yoke' is 'break his control'.

verses.text: Isaac called Jacob and blessed him. Isaac gave him this command: Do not marry a Canaanite woman.
Go to Paddan Aram, to the house of Bethuel, your mother's father. Take a wife from the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother.
May God Almighty bless you. May He give you many children. May He make you the father of many peoples.
May God give you and your descendants the blessing He gave Abraham. May you own the land where you now live as a stranger. God gave that land to Abraham.
So Isaac sent Jacob away. Jacob went to Paddan Aram, to Laban son of Bethuel the Aramean. Laban was the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.
Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob. Isaac had sent Jacob to Paddan Aram to find a wife there. Esau saw that Isaac had commanded Jacob: Do not marry a Canaanite woman.
Esau saw that Jacob had obeyed his father and mother and had gone to Paddan Aram.
Esau saw that the Canaanite women did not please his father Isaac.
So Esau went to Ishmael and married Ishmael's daughter Mahalath. She was the sister of Nebajoth. Esau already had other wives.
Jacob left Beersheba and set out for Haran.
Jacob came to a place and stayed there for the night. The sun had set. He took one of the stones there and put it under his head. Then he lay down to sleep.
Jacob dreamed. He saw a ladder standing on the earth, and its top reached up to heaven. The angels of God were going up and down on the ladder.
The LORD stood above the ladder and said: I am the LORD, the God of your father Abraham. I am also the God of Isaac. I will give you and your descendants the land where you are lying.

Your descendants will be as many as the dust of the earth. They will spread out to the west and east, to the north and south. All the families on earth will be blessed through you and your descendants.
I am with you. I will watch over you wherever you go. I will bring you back to this land. I will not leave you until I have done what I promised you.
Jacob woke up from his sleep. He said: The LORD is in this place, and I did not know it.
Jacob was afraid and said: This place is awesome. This is the house of God. This is the gate of heaven.
Early the next morning Jacob took the stone he had put under his head. He set it up as a pillar and poured oil on top of it.
Jacob named that place Bethel, which means House of God. Before that, the city was called Luz.
Then Jacob made a promise. Jacob said: Suppose God is with me and watches over me on this journey. Suppose God gives me food to eat and clothes to wear.
Suppose God brings me back safely to my father's house. Then the LORD will be my God.
This stone that I have set up as a pillar will be God's house. Of everything You give me, I will give You a tenth.

28.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Check: verse 3 'God Almighty' is El Shaddai; verse 12 'angels' is kept; verse 17 'dreadful' is 'awesome' (without an exclamation mark); verse 19 'Bethel' means House of God; verses 20-22 are one promise, written with 'Suppose' because the KJV 'if' runs across verses 20-21; 'tenth' is the KJV 'tenth'.

verses.text: Jacob continued his journey and came to the land of the eastern peoples.
Jacob saw a well in a field. There were 3 flocks of sheep lying beside it. The flocks were given water from that well. A large stone covered the mouth of the well.
When all the flocks were gathered there, the shepherds rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well. They gave the sheep water. Then they put the stone back.
Jacob asked the shepherds: My brothers, where are you from? They answered: We are from Haran.
Jacob asked them: Do you know Laban, the grandson of Nahor? They answered: We know him.
Jacob asked them: Is he well? They answered: He is well. Look, his daughter Rachel is coming with the sheep.
Jacob said: Look, the sun is still high. It is not time to gather the animals. Give the sheep water and take them back to eat grass.
They answered: We cannot do that until all the flocks are gathered. Then the stone will be rolled away from the well. We will give the sheep water.
While Jacob was still talking with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep, because she took care of them.
Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of his mother's brother Laban, with Laban's sheep. Jacob went to the well and rolled the stone away. Then Jacob gave Laban's sheep water.
Jacob kissed Rachel and cried out loud.
Jacob told Rachel that he was a relative of her father and the son of Rebekah. So Rachel ran and told her father.
Laban heard the news about his sister's son Jacob. Laban ran to meet him. Laban hugged Jacob and kissed him. Laban brought Jacob to his house. Jacob told Laban everything that had happened.
Laban said to Jacob: You are my own flesh and blood. So Jacob stayed with Laban for a month.
Then Laban said to Jacob: You are my relative, but you should not work for me for nothing. Tell me what pay you want.
Laban had 2 daughters. The older daughter was named Leah, and the younger daughter was named Rachel.
Leah had weak eyes, but Rachel was beautiful and lovely to look at.
Jacob loved Rachel. Jacob said: I will work for you 7 years for your younger daughter Rachel.
Laban said: It is better for me to give her to you than to another man. Stay here with me.
So Jacob worked 7 years for Rachel. The years seemed like only a few days to him, because he loved her so much.
Then Jacob said to Laban: My time of work is finished. Give me my wife so that I can marry her.
Laban invited all the people of that place and gave a feast.
That evening Laban took his daughter Leah and brought her to Jacob. Jacob slept with her.
Laban gave his servant Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her servant.
In the morning Jacob saw that it was Leah. Jacob said to Laban: What have you done to me? I worked for Rachel. Why did you trick me?
Laban answered: In our country it is not the custom to give the younger daughter in marriage before the older.
Finish the wedding week with Leah. Then we will give you Rachel also. You must work for me 7 more years.
Jacob did that. He finished the week with Leah. Then Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife.
Laban gave his servant Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her servant.
Jacob slept with Rachel also. Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah. He worked for Laban 7 more years.
The LORD saw that Jacob did not love Leah, so the LORD let Leah have children. But Rachel had no children.
Leah became pregnant and had a son. She named him Reuben, which sounds like the words: See, a son. She said: The LORD has seen my trouble. Now my husband will love me.
Leah became pregnant again and had a son. She said: The LORD heard that I am not loved, so He gave me this son also. She named him Simeon, which sounds like the word for Heard.
Leah became pregnant again and had a son. She said: Now my husband will stay close to me, because I have given him 3 sons. So she named him Levi, which sounds like the word for Stay Close.
Leah became pregnant again and had a son. She said: This time I will praise the LORD. So she named him Judah, which sounds like the word for Praise. Then Leah stopped having children.

29.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Hard chapter: verses 21-25 (the wedding night and the trick on Jacob) and verses 31-35 (Leah's sons and the name meanings) need careful review. Check: 'tender eyed' (verse 17) is 'weak eyes'; 'went in unto' is 'slept with'; 'hated' (verse 31) is rendered 'did not love'; the meanings of Reuben, Simeon, Levi and Judah (verses 32-35) are given as sounds-like words.

verses.text: Rachel saw that she had given Jacob no children, and she became jealous of her sister Leah. Rachel said to Jacob: Give me children, or I will die.
Jacob became angry with Rachel. He said: Am I God? God is the One who has kept you from having children.
Rachel said: Here is my servant Bilhah. Sleep with her. She will have a child for me, and I will have a family through her.
So Rachel gave her servant Bilhah to Jacob as a wife. Jacob slept with Bilhah.
Bilhah became pregnant and had a son for Jacob.
Rachel said: God has judged in my favor. God has heard my prayer and given me a son. So she named him Dan, which sounds like the word for Judged.
Rachel's servant Bilhah became pregnant again and had a 2nd son for Jacob.
Rachel said: I have had a great struggle with my sister, and I have won. So she named him Naphtali, which sounds like the word for My Struggle.
Leah saw that she had stopped having children. So Leah took her servant Zilpah and gave her to Jacob as a wife.
Leah's servant Zilpah had a son for Jacob.
Leah said: How fortunate I am. So she named him Gad, which sounds like the word for Fortune.
Leah's servant Zilpah had a 2nd son for Jacob.
Leah said: How happy I am. Women will call me happy. So she named him Asher, which sounds like the word for Happy.

During the wheat harvest, Reuben went out to the field and found some mandrakes, plants that people believed helped women have children. Reuben brought them to his mother Leah. Rachel said to Leah: Please give me some of your son's mandrakes.
Leah answered: Is it not enough that you took my husband? Now you want to take my son's mandrakes too. Rachel said: Then Jacob may sleep with you tonight, if you give me your son's mandrakes.

That evening Jacob came in from the field. Leah went out to meet him and said: You must sleep with me tonight, because I have paid for you with my son's mandrakes. So Jacob slept with Leah that night.
God listened to Leah. Leah became pregnant and had a 5th son for Jacob.
Leah said: God has rewarded me, because I gave my servant to my husband. So she named him Issachar, which sounds like the word for Reward.
Leah became pregnant again and had a 6th son for Jacob.
Leah said: God has given me a good gift. Now my husband will honor me, because I have given him 6 sons. So she named him Zebulun, which sounds like the word for Honor.
After that, Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.
Then God remembered Rachel. God listened to her and let her have children.
Rachel became pregnant and had a son. She said: God has taken away my shame.
Rachel named him Joseph, which sounds like the words May He Add. She said: May the LORD give me another son.
After Rachel had Joseph, Jacob said to Laban: Send me away. I want to go back to my own home and my own country.
Give me my wives and my children, whom I worked for. Let me go. You know how hard I have worked for you.
Laban said to Jacob: Please stay, if I have pleased you. I have learned by signs that the LORD has blessed me because of you.
Laban said: Tell me what pay you want, and I will give it to you.
Jacob said to Laban: You know how I have worked for you. You know how your animals have done well with me.
You had little before I came, and now you have much. The LORD has blessed you everywhere I worked. But when can I work for my own family?
Laban asked: What should I give you? Jacob answered: Do not give me anything. But do this one thing for me, and I will feed and take care of your flocks again.
Let me walk through all your flocks today. I will take out every speckled and spotted sheep, every dark lamb and every spotted and speckled goat. That will be my pay.
Later you can check my pay. My honesty will speak for me. If I have any goat that is not speckled or spotted, or any lamb that is not dark, it was stolen.
Laban said: Agreed. Let it be as you say.
That same day Laban took out all the striped and spotted male goats and all the speckled and spotted female goats. He also took out all the dark lambs. Laban put them in the care of his sons.
Laban put a distance of 3 days' journey between himself and Jacob. Jacob took care of the rest of Laban's flocks.
Jacob took fresh branches from poplar, almond and plane trees. He peeled off strips of bark so that the white wood showed on the branches.
Jacob put the peeled branches in front of the flocks, in the water troughs where the flocks came to drink. The flocks mated when they came to drink.
The flocks mated in front of the branches. Their young were striped, speckled and spotted.

Jacob separated the young animals from the rest. He made the other animals face the striped and dark animals in Laban's flock. Jacob made separate flocks for himself and did not put them with Laban's animals.
Whenever the stronger animals were mating, Jacob put the branches in the troughs where the animals could see them.
But when the animals were weak, Jacob did not put the branches there. So the weak animals went to Laban, and the strong animals went to Jacob.
Jacob became very rich. He had large flocks, male and female servants, camels and donkeys.

verses.text: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were saying: Jacob has taken everything our father owned. Jacob got all his wealth from our father.
Jacob saw that Laban was not friendly to him as he had been before.
Then the LORD said to Jacob: Go back to the land of your fathers and your relatives. I will be with you.
Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to come to the field where his flocks were.
Jacob said to them: I see that your father is not friendly to me as he was before. But the God of my father has been with me.
You know that I have worked for your father with all my strength.
Your father has cheated me. He changed my pay 10 times. But God did not let him harm me.
When Laban said: The speckled animals will be your pay, all the flock had speckled young. When Laban said: The striped animals will be your pay, all the flock had striped young.
So God has taken your father's animals and given them to me.
At the time when the flocks were mating, I had a dream. I saw that the male goats mating with the flock were striped, speckled and spotted.
In the dream the angel of God said to me: Jacob. I answered: Here I am.
The angel said: Look up and see. All the male goats mating with the flock are striped, speckled and spotted. I have seen everything Laban has done to you.
I am the God of Bethel, where you poured oil on a pillar and made a promise to Me. Now leave this land and go back to the land where you were born.
Rachel and Leah answered Jacob: Do we still have any share in our father's property?
Our father treats us like strangers. He sold us, and he has spent all the money paid for us.
All the wealth that God took from our father belongs to us and our children. Do whatever God has told you.
Then Jacob put his children and his wives on camels.
Jacob drove ahead all his animals and all the goods he had gained in Paddan Aram. He set out for the land of Canaan, to his father Isaac.
Laban had gone to cut the wool from his sheep. While he was gone, Rachel stole her father's household gods.
Jacob tricked Laban the Aramean by not telling him that he was running away.
Jacob ran away with everything he owned. He crossed the Euphrates River and headed for the hill country of Gilead.
On the 3rd day Laban was told that Jacob had run away.
Laban took his relatives and chased Jacob for 7 days. Laban caught up with Jacob in the hill country of Gilead.
That night God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream and said: Be careful. Do not say anything to Jacob, good or bad.
Laban caught up with Jacob. Jacob had set up his tent in the hill country. Laban and his relatives set up their tents in the hill country of Gilead too.
Laban said to Jacob: What have you done? You tricked me. You took my daughters away like prisoners of war.
Why did you run away secretly and trick me? Why did you not tell me? I would have sent you off with joy and singing, with tambourines and harps.
You did not let me kiss my grandchildren and my daughters goodbye. You were foolish.
I have the power to harm you. But last night the God of your father said to me: Be careful. Do not say anything to Jacob, good or bad.
You left because you wanted so much to go back to your father's house. But why did you steal my gods?
Jacob answered Laban: I was afraid. I thought you would take your daughters from me by force.
But if you find your gods with anyone here, that person will not live. Look at what I have in front of our relatives, and take whatever is yours. Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen the gods.
Laban went into Jacob's tent, then Leah's tent, then the tent of the 2 servant women. He found nothing. Then he went into Rachel's tent.
Rachel had taken the household gods and put them in the camel saddle. She was sitting on them. Laban searched the whole tent but found nothing.
Rachel said to her father: Please do not be angry, sir, that I cannot stand up in front of you. I am having my monthly period. So Laban searched but did not find the household gods.
Jacob became angry and scolded Laban. Jacob said: What crime have I done? What sin have I done, that you chase me like this?
You have searched through everything I own. What did you find that belongs to your household? Put it here in front of our relatives. Let them judge between us.
I have been with you 20 years. Your female sheep and goats have not lost their young. I have not eaten the rams of your flocks.
When wild animals killed one of your animals, I did not bring it to you. I paid for the loss myself. You made me pay for every animal stolen by day or by night.
In the daytime the heat wore me out, and at night the cold did. I could hardly sleep.
I was in your household for 20 years. I worked 14 years for your 2 daughters and 6 years for your flocks. You changed my pay 10 times.

The God of my father, the God of Abraham, the God whom Isaac fears, was with me. If He had not been, you would have sent me away with nothing. God saw my trouble and my hard work, and last night He told you that you were wrong.

Laban answered Jacob: These women are my daughters. These children are my children. These flocks are my flocks. All you see belongs to me. But what can I do today about my daughters or the children they have had?
Come, let us make an agreement, you and I. Let it be a witness between us.
So Jacob took a stone and set it up as a pillar.
Jacob said to his relatives: Gather stones. They took stones and made a pile. They ate a meal there by the pile.
Laban named the pile Jegar Sahadutha. Jacob named it Galeed. Both names mean Pile of Witness.
Laban said: This pile is a witness between you and me today. That is why it was named Galeed.
It was also named Mizpah, which means Watchtower, because Laban said: May the LORD watch over you and me when we are away from each other.
If you mistreat my daughters or marry other wives, no one may be with us. But remember that God is a witness between you and me.
Laban said to Jacob: Here is this pile, and here is the pillar I have set up between you and me.
This pile is a witness, and this pillar is a witness. I will not go past this pile to harm you. You will not go past this pile and this pillar to harm me.
May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us. Jacob made an oath in the name of the God whom his father Isaac feared.
Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain and invited his relatives to eat a meal. They ate and spent the night on the mountain.
Early the next morning Laban kissed his grandchildren and his daughters and blessed them. Then Laban left and went back home.

31.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Check: 'teraphim' is 'household gods'; 'the Fear of Isaac' (verses 42, 53) is 'the God whom Isaac fears'; 'covenant' (verse 44) is 'agreement'; 'Galeed' and 'Jegar Sahadutha' both mean Pile of Witness; 'Mizpah' means Watchtower.

verses.text: Jacob went on and there were angels of God who came to Jacob.
When Jacob saw the angels, Jacob said: This is a camp of God's soldiers. Jacob named that place Mahanaim, which means Two Camps.
Jacob sent a message to his brother Esau. Esau was in the land of Seir, the country of Edom.
Jacob told the men to tell his brother Esau: Sir, I am your servant Jacob. I have lived with Laban all these years.
Now I have oxen, donkeys, sheep, goats, male servants and female servants. I am sending you this message. I hope you will be friendly and accept me back.
When the messengers came back to Jacob, they said to Jacob: We went to your brother Esau. Esau is coming to meet you, and Esau has 400 men with him.
Jacob became afraid and very worried. Jacob divided all the people who were with Jacob into 2 groups. Jacob also divided all the sheep, goats, oxen and camels.
Jacob said: If Esau attacks one group, then the other group can flee.
Jacob prayed to God and said: God of my grandfather Abraham, God of my father Isaac, LORD, You told me to go back to my land and to my family. You said that You would be good to me.
I am not worthy of all Your kindness. You have done everything You promised me. When I first crossed the Jordan River, I owned nothing but my walking stick. Now I own enough to have 2 full camps.
Please protect me from my brother Esau, because I am afraid of Esau. I am afraid that Esau will attack me and the women and children.
You have promised and said to me: I will be good to Jacob. I will make your descendants as many as the grains of sand of the sea. There will be so many that no one will be able to count them.
Jacob slept there that night. Jacob took some of his animals and sent a gift to his brother Esau.
Jacob's gift was 200 female goats and 20 male goats, 200 female sheep and 20 male sheep.
Jacob also sent 30 nursing camels and their calves, 40 cows and 10 bulls, and 20 female donkeys and 10 young donkeys.
Jacob gave the animals to his servants. Jacob gave a flock of animals to each servant and told the servants: Walk ahead of me, but keep each flock separate.
Jacob told the 1st servant: When my brother Esau comes to you and asks you whose servant you are, where you are going and whose animals these are,
you must tell Esau: Sir, they belong to your servant Jacob. They are a gift that Jacob sends to you, Esau. Jacob is also coming. Jacob is behind us.
Jacob said the same to the 2nd servant and the 3rd servant, and to all the other servants who followed the flocks. Jacob told the servants what they must say to Esau when they found him.

They also had to say to Esau: Your servant Jacob is also coming. Jacob is behind us. Jacob said to himself: I will make peace with Esau by sending this gift ahead of me. When I see Esau face to face, maybe Esau will accept me.
Jacob first sent the gifts to Esau, and Jacob stayed that night in the camp.
Jacob got up that night. Jacob took his 2 wives, his 2 servant women and his 11 sons, and they went through the Jabbok River.
Jacob sent them through the river and then Jacob also sent his animals through the river.
Jacob stayed behind, alone. A man came and wrestled with Jacob until just before the sun came up the next day.
The man saw that he could not defeat Jacob. The man touched the hollow of Jacob's thigh. Jacob's thigh was thrown out of joint.
The man said to Jacob: Let me go, because the sun is coming up and it is almost day. But Jacob said to the man: I will not let you go unless you bless me.
The man asked Jacob: What is your name? Jacob said: Jacob.
The man said: Your name will no longer be Jacob. From now on you will be Israel. This is because you have wrestled with God and with people, and you have won.
Jacob asked: Please tell me your name. The man said: Why do you ask what my name is? The man blessed Jacob there.
Jacob named that place Peniel, which means Face of God. Jacob said: At this place, I saw God face to face, but my life was spared.
The sun came up when Jacob went away from Peniel. Jacob could not walk well because his thigh was hurt.
That is why the Israelites never eat the sinew in the hollow of an animal's thigh. The man touched the hollow of Jacob's thigh.

32.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with pronouns replaced by the nouns they refer to and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs.

verses.text: Jacob looked up and saw Esau coming with 400 men. So Jacob divided his children among Leah, Rachel and the 2 servant women.
Jacob put the servant women and their children in front. He put Leah and her children next. He put Rachel and Joseph last.
Jacob himself went ahead of them. He bowed down to the ground 7 times as he came near his brother Esau.
But Esau ran to meet Jacob. Esau hugged him and kissed him, and they both cried.
Esau looked up and saw the women and children. Esau asked: Who are these people with you? Jacob answered: They are the children God has kindly given to me, your servant.
Then the servant women and their children came near and bowed down.
Leah and her children came near and bowed down. Last, Joseph and Rachel came near and bowed down.
Esau asked: What was the meaning of all those animals I met? Jacob answered: They were a gift to win your favor, sir.
Esau said: I have plenty, my brother. Keep what you have.
Jacob said: No, please. If I have found favor with you, accept my gift. When I see your face, it is like seeing the face of God, because you have welcomed me so kindly.
Please accept the gift I brought to you. God has been kind to me, and I have all I need. Jacob urged Esau, and Esau accepted the gift.
Esau said: Let us travel on. I will go along with you.
Jacob said to Esau: Sir, you know that the children are young. I must also care for the sheep and farm animals that have young ones. If they are driven too hard for one day, all the animals will die.
Please go on ahead of me, sir. I will move slowly, at the pace of the animals and the children. I will come to you in Seir.
Esau said: Let me leave some of my men with you. Jacob asked: Why do that? Let me just find favor with you, sir.
So that day Esau started back to Seir.
But Jacob went to Succoth. There Jacob built a house for himself and shelters for his animals. That is why the place was named Succoth, which means Shelters.
Jacob arrived safely at the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan. He set up his camp near the city.
Jacob bought the piece of land where he had set up his tent. He bought it from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for 100 pieces of silver.
There Jacob built an altar and named it El Elohe Israel, which means God, the God of Israel.

33.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Check: verse 10 'as though I had seen the face of God' is kept; verse 11 'blessing' is 'gift'; verse 13 'flocks and herds' is 'sheep and farm animals'; 'Succoth' means Shelters.

verses.text: Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, went out to visit the women of the land.
Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the ruler of that land, saw Dinah. He took her and forced her to sleep with him.
Shechem loved Dinah, the daughter of Jacob. He loved the young woman and spoke kindly to her.
Shechem said to his father Hamor: Get me this young woman as my wife.
Jacob heard that Shechem had made his daughter Dinah unclean. His sons were in the field with the animals, so Jacob kept quiet until they came home.
Shechem's father Hamor went out to talk with Jacob.

Jacob's sons came in from the field when they heard what had happened. The men were hurt and very angry. Shechem had done a shameful thing in Israel by sleeping with Jacob's daughter. That should never be done.
Hamor said to them: My son Shechem wants your daughter very much. Please give her to him as his wife.
Let us marry each other's children. Give us your daughters, and take our daughters for yourselves.
Live among us. The land is open to you. Live in it, trade in it and buy property in it.
Shechem said to Dinah's father and brothers: Let me find favor with you. I will give you whatever you ask.
Ask as high a price as you like, and I will pay it. Only give me the young woman as my wife.
Jacob's sons answered Shechem and his father Hamor with a trick, because Shechem had made their sister Dinah unclean.
They said: We cannot give our sister to a man who is not circumcised. That would bring shame on us.
We will agree to this only on one condition: Every male among you must be circumcised, as we are.
Then we will give you our daughters, and we will take your daughters. We will live among you and be united with you.
But if you will not listen and be circumcised, we will take our sister and leave.
Their words pleased Hamor and his son Shechem.
The young man did not wait to do this, because he loved Jacob's daughter. Shechem was the most honored man in his family.
Hamor and his son Shechem went to the gate of their city. They spoke to the men of the city.
They said: These men are friendly to us. Let them live in our land and trade in it. The land has plenty of room for them. Let us marry their daughters, and let them marry ours.
But these men will agree to live with us and be united with us only on one condition: Every male among us must be circumcised, as they are.
Their animals, their property and all their other animals will become ours. Only let us agree to their terms, and they will live among us.
All the men who went out of the city gate agreed with Hamor and his son Shechem. Every male was circumcised.

On the 3rd day, while all the men were still in pain, 2 of Jacob's sons attacked the city. They were Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers. They took their swords, attacked the city while it was unprepared and killed every male.
They killed Hamor and his son Shechem with their swords. They took Dinah out of Shechem's house and left.
Jacob's other sons came to the dead bodies and took everything from the city, because the city's men had made their sister unclean.
They took the sheep, the farm animals and the donkeys. They took everything in the city and in the fields.
They took all the wealth, all the women and children, and everything in the houses.

Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi: You have brought trouble on me. You have made me hated by the Canaanites and Perizzites who live in this land. We are few in number. If they join together and attack me, my whole family will be destroyed.
But Simeon and Levi answered: Should Shechem treat our sister like a prostitute?

34.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Hard chapter: verse 2 ('lay with her, and defiled her') and the revenge in verses 25-29 need careful review. Check: 'defiled' is 'made unclean'; verse 16 'become one people' is 'be united'; verse 25 'sore' is 'in pain'; verse 31 is kept as the sons' harsh question.

verses.text: God said to Jacob: Go up to Bethel and live there. Build an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you ran away from your brother Esau.
Jacob said to his family and to everyone with him: Get rid of the foreign gods that you have. Make yourselves clean, and change your clothes.
Let us go up to Bethel. There I will build an altar to the God who answered me when I was in trouble. God has been with me everywhere I went.
So the people gave Jacob all their foreign gods and their earrings. Jacob buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.
Then they set out. A great fear from God came over the towns around them, so no one chased Jacob's sons.
Jacob and all the people with him came to Luz, which is Bethel, in the land of Canaan.
Jacob built an altar there. He named the place El Bethel, which means God of Bethel, because God had appeared to him there when he ran away from his brother.
Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died. She was buried under the oak tree below Bethel. So that tree was named Allon Bacuth, which means Oak of Weeping.
After Jacob came back from Paddan Aram, God appeared to him again and blessed him.
God said to him: Your name is Jacob. You will no longer be called Jacob. Your name will be Israel. So God named him Israel.
God said to him: I am God Almighty. Have many children and grow in number. A nation will come from you, and a group of nations. Kings will be born in your family.
I gave this land to Abraham and Isaac. I will give it to you and to your descendants after you.
Then God went up from Jacob, from the place where He had spoken with him.
Jacob set up a stone pillar at the place where God had spoken with him. He poured a drink offering and oil on it.
Jacob named that place where God spoke with him Bethel.
Then they left Bethel. They were still some distance from Ephrath when Rachel began to give birth. Her labor was very hard.
During the hard labor the midwife said to Rachel: Do not be afraid, because you have another son.
Rachel was dying. As she took her last breath, she named her son Ben Oni, which means Son of My Trouble. But his father named him Benjamin, which means Son of My Right Hand.
So Rachel died. She was buried on the road to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.
Jacob set up a pillar over her grave. That pillar marks Rachel's grave to this day.
Israel moved on and set up his tent beyond the tower of Eder.
While Israel lived in that land, Reuben slept with Bilhah, his father's wife. Israel heard about it. Jacob had 12 sons.
The sons of Leah were Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, then Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar and Zebulun.
The sons of Rachel were Joseph and Benjamin.
The sons of Rachel's servant Bilhah were Dan and Naphtali.
The sons of Leah's servant Zilpah were Gad and Asher. These were the sons born to Jacob in Paddan Aram.
Jacob came home to his father Isaac at Mamre, near Kiriath Arba, which is Hebron. Abraham and Isaac had lived there.
Isaac lived 180 years.
Isaac died at a good old age, after a full life. Isaac joined his people. His sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

35.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Check: verse 11 'God Almighty' is El Shaddai; verse 22 'concubine' is 'wife'; verse 18 'Benoni' and 'Benjamin' meanings are given; verse 29 'gathered unto his people' is 'joined his people'.

verses.text: This is the family record of Esau, who is also called Edom.
Esau married women from the land of Canaan. They were Adah daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Oholibamah daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite.
Esau also married Basemath daughter of Ishmael, the sister of Nebajoth.
Adah had a son named Eliphaz. Basemath had a son named Reuel.
Oholibamah had sons named Jeush, Jalam and Korah. These were Esau's sons, born in the land of Canaan.

Esau took his wives, his sons and daughters, and everyone in his household. He took his animals and all his property, which he had gotten in Canaan. Then Esau moved to a land some distance from his brother Jacob.
Esau and Jacob owned too much to live together. The land where they lived as strangers could not feed all their animals.
So Esau, who is also called Edom, lived in the hill country of Seir.
This is the family record of Esau, the father of the Edomites, in the hill country of Seir.
These are the names of Esau's sons. Eliphaz was the son of Esau's wife Adah. Reuel was the son of Esau's wife Basemath.
The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam and Kenaz.
Timna was a wife of Esau's son Eliphaz. She had a son named Amalek. These were the grandsons of Esau's wife Adah.
The sons of Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah. These were the grandsons of Esau's wife Basemath.
Esau's wife Oholibamah was the daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon. She had sons named Jeush, Jalam and Korah.
These were the chiefs among Esau's descendants. The sons of Eliphaz, Esau's oldest son, were chiefs. They were Teman, Omar, Zepho and Kenaz.
Korah, Gatam and Amalek were also chiefs. These were the chiefs from Eliphaz in the land of Edom. They were the grandsons of Adah.
The sons of Esau's son Reuel were chiefs Nahath, Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah. These were the chiefs from Reuel in the land of Edom. They were the grandsons of Esau's wife Basemath.
The sons of Esau's wife Oholibamah were chiefs Jeush, Jalam and Korah. These were the chiefs from Esau's wife Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah.
These were the sons of Esau, who is also called Edom, and these were their chiefs.
These were the sons of Seir the Horite, who lived in that land. They were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon and Anah.
Dishon, Ezer and Dishan were also sons of Seir. These were the chiefs of the Horites, the sons of Seir, in the land of Edom.
The sons of Lotan were Hori and Heman. Lotan's sister was Timna.
The sons of Shobal were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho and Onam.
The sons of Zibeon were Aiah and Anah. This is the Anah who found the hot springs in the desert while he was caring for his father Zibeon's donkeys.
The children of Anah were Dishon and Oholibamah, who was Anah's daughter.
The sons of Dishon were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran and Keran.
The sons of Ezer were Bilhan, Zaavan and Akan.
The sons of Dishan were Uz and Aran.
These were the chiefs of the Horites. They were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon and Anah.
Dishon, Ezer and Dishan were also chiefs. These were the chiefs of the Horites, by their clans in the land of Seir.
These were the kings who ruled in the land of Edom before any king ruled the Israelites.
Bela son of Beor became king of Edom. His city was named Dinhabah.
When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah became king.
When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites became king.
When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad became king. Hadad defeated the Midianites in the country of Moab. His city was named Avith.
When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah became king.
When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth on the river became king.
When Shaul died, Baal Hanan son of Acbor became king.
When Baal Hanan died, Hadar became king. His city was named Pau. His wife was named Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred and the granddaughter of Mezahab.
These are the names of the chiefs who came from Esau, by their clans and their places. They were Timna, Alvah and Jetheth.
Oholibamah, Elah and Pinon were also chiefs.
Kenaz, Teman and Mibzar were also chiefs.
Magdiel and Iram were also chiefs. These were all the chiefs of Edom, by their settlements in the land they owned. This was Esau, the father of the Edomites.

36.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. A family list: names follow the KJV spellings. verses.text: Jacob lived in the land of Canaan where his father Isaac had been a stranger before.

Here is the story of Jacob's family. Joseph was 17 years old. Joseph looked after his father's sheep and goats with his brothers. They were the sons of his father's wives Bilhah and Zilpah. Joseph told his father about the bad things that his brothers did.
Jacob's other name was Israel. Jacob loved Joseph more than all his other sons. Joseph was born when Jacob was old. Jacob gave Joseph a special coat that had many colors.
Joseph's brothers saw that their father, Jacob, loved Joseph more than them, and they hated Joseph. Joseph's brothers did not want to say anything good about Joseph.
One night Joseph dreamed and Joseph told his brothers what Joseph had dreamed. Then the brothers hated Joseph even more.
Joseph said to his brothers: Please listen to the dream I had.
Joseph said: We were tying bundles of wheat in the field. My bundle of wheat stood upright. Your bundles of wheat stood around my bundle and bowed down to it.
Joseph's brothers said to Joseph: Do you really think that you will be king and rule over us? Joseph's brothers hated Joseph even more after Joseph told the brothers about the dream.
Joseph dreamed another dream and told his brothers: I dreamed again. This time the sun, the moon and 11 stars bowed down to me.
Joseph told his father and his brothers about the dream. His father scolded Joseph and said: What kind of dream is this? Will your mother, your brothers and I all bow down to the ground before you?
Joseph's brothers were jealous of Joseph, but Joseph's father kept the matter in mind.
Joseph's brothers had to look after their father's sheep and goats near the town of Shechem.
Jacob said to Joseph: Your brothers are looking after the sheep and goats near the town of Shechem. You must go to them. Joseph said: Yes, Father, I will go.

Jacob told Joseph: Go and see if everything is well with your brothers and with the sheep and goats. Come back and tell me everything. So Jacob sent Joseph from the Hebron Valley. Joseph went to the town of Shechem.
Joseph was walking in the field when a man saw Joseph. The man asked Joseph: What are you looking for?
Joseph said to the man: I am looking for my brothers. Do you know where they are with their sheep and goats? If you know, please tell me.
The man said: They are no longer here. They went away from here. They said that they were going to Dothan. Joseph followed his brothers and found them in Dothan.
While Joseph was still far away, the brothers saw Joseph coming. Before Joseph reached them, the brothers made a plan to kill Joseph.
Joseph's brothers said to each other: Look, here comes the big dreamer.
Joseph's brothers said: Let us kill Joseph and throw him into a pit. We can tell our father that a wild animal killed Joseph. Then we will show that all of his dreams meant nothing.
When Joseph's brothers told Reuben about it, Reuben wanted to save Joseph. Reuben said: No, we must not kill Joseph.

Reuben said to the brothers: Do not shed blood. Put Joseph into this pit in the wilderness, but do not hurt Joseph. Reuben planned to rescue Joseph later. Reuben wanted to bring Joseph back to their father.
When Joseph came to his brothers, they took off his coat of many colors that Joseph was wearing.
Joseph's brothers took Joseph and threw him into a pit that was empty and dry.

Joseph's brothers sat down to eat. They looked up and saw a group of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were carrying many different spices, balm and myrrh. The Ishmaelites wanted to sell their spices in Egypt.
Judah said to his brothers: We will have nothing if we kill our brother Joseph and keep quiet about it.
Let us sell Joseph to the Ishmaelites. We must not kill him. Remember, Joseph is our brother. Judah's brothers agreed with Judah.
The Midianite merchants came near. Joseph's brothers pulled Joseph out of the pit. They sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for 20 pieces of silver. The merchants took Joseph to Egypt.
When Reuben came back to the pit and saw that Joseph was not there, Reuben was very upset and tore his clothes.
Reuben went back to his brothers and asked them: The child is no longer there. Where shall I go?
Joseph's brothers killed a goat and took Joseph's coat and put blood on it.
Joseph's brothers sent Joseph's coat of many colors to their father and said: We found this coat. See if it is your son's coat or not.
Jacob looked at the coat and said: This is my son's coat. A wild animal has eaten Joseph. Joseph has surely been torn to pieces.
Jacob was very sad. Jacob tore his clothes and put on rough cloth. Jacob cried and mourned for Joseph for a long time.
All Jacob's sons and daughters came to comfort Jacob, but Jacob refused to be comforted. Jacob said: I will continue to mourn for Joseph until I die. Jacob cried a lot about Joseph.
The Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and the captain of the palace guard.

37.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with pronouns replaced by the nouns they refer to and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs.

verses.text: About that time Judah left his brothers and went to stay with a man from Adullam named Hirah.
There Judah saw the daughter of a Canaanite man named Shua. Judah married her and slept with her.
She became pregnant and had a son. Judah named him Er.
She became pregnant again and had another son. She named him Onan.
She had another son and named him Shelah. Judah was in Kezib when she had him.
Judah got a wife for his oldest son Er. Her name was Tamar.
But Judah's oldest son Er did wicked things, and the LORD saw it. So the LORD let Er die.
Then Judah said to Onan: Sleep with your brother's wife. Do your duty as her brother-in-law, and have a child for your brother.
Onan knew the child would not be his. So when Onan slept with his brother's wife, he spilled his seed on the ground. He did not want to give his brother a child.
What Onan did was wicked, and the LORD saw it. So the LORD let Onan die also.

Then Judah said to his daughter-in-law Tamar: Live as a widow in your father's house until my son Shelah grows up. Judah was afraid that Shelah would die like his brothers. So Tamar went to live in her father's house.
After a long time Judah's wife, the daughter of Shua, died. When Judah finished mourning, he went up to Timnah to cut the wool from his sheep. His friend Hirah from Adullam went with him.
Someone told Tamar: Your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to cut the wool from his sheep.

Tamar took off her widow's clothes and covered her face with a veil. She sat down at the entrance to Enaim, on the road to Timnah. She saw that Shelah had grown up, but she had not been given to him as his wife.
Judah saw Tamar and thought she was a prostitute, because she had covered her face.
Judah did not know she was his daughter-in-law. He went over to her by the road and said: Come, let me sleep with you. She asked: What will you give me for sleeping with you?
Judah said: I will send you a young goat from my flock. She asked: Will you give me something to hold until you send it?
Judah asked: What should I give you to hold? She answered: Your seal and its cord, and the walking stick in your hand. Judah gave them to her and slept with her. Tamar became pregnant.
Then Tamar got up and left. She took off her veil and put on her widow's clothes again.
Judah sent the young goat by his friend Hirah to get back the things he had given the woman. But Hirah could not find her.
Hirah asked the men of that place: Where is the temple prostitute who was beside the road at Enaim? They answered: There has never been a temple prostitute here.
So Hirah went back to Judah and said: I could not find her. The men of that place said: There has never been a temple prostitute here.
Judah said: Let her keep what she has, or people will laugh at us. I did send the young goat, but you could not find her.
About 3 months later Judah was told: Your daughter-in-law Tamar has acted like a prostitute, and she is pregnant. Judah said: Bring her out and burn her.
As Tamar was being brought out, she sent a message to her father-in-law: The man who owns these things made me pregnant. Please look. Whose seal, cord and walking stick are these?
Judah knew them. He said: Tamar is more right than I am, because I did not give her to my son Shelah. Judah never slept with her again.
When Tamar was ready to give birth, there were twin boys in her body.
As she gave birth, one baby put out his hand. The midwife tied a red thread on his hand and said: This one came out first.
But the baby pulled his hand back, and his brother came out first. The midwife said: You have broken out first. So he was named Perez, which means Breaking Out.
Then his brother came out, the one with the red thread on his hand. He was named Zerah.

38.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Hard chapter: verses 8-10 (Onan), 14-18 and 24-26 (Tamar and Judah) need careful review. Check: 'went in unto' is 'slept with'; 'harlot' is 'prostitute'; verse 21 'harlot' is the Hebrew for a temple prostitute; verse 9 is rendered plainly; 'Perez' means Breaking Out.

verses.text: Joseph was taken down to Egypt. An Egyptian named Potiphar bought him from the Ishmaelites who had brought him there. Potiphar was an officer of Pharaoh and the captain of the guard.
The LORD was with Joseph, and Joseph did well. Joseph lived in the house of his Egyptian master.
Potiphar saw that the LORD was with Joseph. Potiphar saw that the LORD gave Joseph success in everything he did.
Joseph pleased Potiphar and became his servant. Potiphar put Joseph in charge of his house and gave him care of everything he owned.
From the time Potiphar put Joseph in charge, the LORD blessed the Egyptian's house because of Joseph. The blessing of the LORD was on everything Potiphar owned, in the house and in the field.
Potiphar left everything he owned in Joseph's care. With Joseph there, Potiphar worried about nothing except the food he ate. Joseph was strong and very handsome.
After a while Potiphar's wife looked at Joseph with desire. She said: Sleep with me.
But Joseph refused. He said to Potiphar's wife: My master does not worry about anything in the house, because I am here. He has put everything he owns in my care.
No one in this house is greater than I am. My master has kept nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. How could I do this great evil and sin against God?
She spoke to Joseph day after day, but Joseph refused to sleep with her or even to be with her.
One day Joseph went into the house to do his work. None of the household servants were inside.
Potiphar's wife grabbed Joseph by his coat and said: Sleep with me. But Joseph left his coat in her hand and ran out of the house.
She saw that Joseph had left his coat in her hand and had run out of the house.
She called to the servants of her house and said: Look, my husband has brought this Hebrew to make fools of us. He came in to sleep with me, but I screamed loudly.
When he heard me scream, he left his coat beside me and ran out of the house.
Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat beside her until her husband came home.
Then she told Potiphar the same story: The Hebrew servant you brought us came in to make fun of me.
But when I screamed, he left his coat beside me and ran out of the house.
Potiphar heard what his wife said to him: This is how your servant treated me. Potiphar became very angry.
Joseph's master took Joseph and put him in prison, the place where the king's prisoners were kept. Joseph stayed there in prison.
But the LORD was with Joseph. The LORD showed him kindness and gave him favor with the man in charge of the prison.
The man in charge of the prison put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners. Joseph was in charge of everything that was done there.
The man in charge of the prison did not worry about anything in Joseph's care, because the LORD was with Joseph. The LORD gave Joseph success in everything he did.

39.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Hard verses: 7, 12 (Potiphar's wife). Check: 'lie with me' is 'sleep with me'; 'cast her eyes upon Joseph' is 'looked at Joseph with desire'; 'garment' is 'coat'.

verses.text: Some time later, the king of Egypt's cupbearer and baker made their master angry. The cupbearer was the servant who served the king's wine.
Pharaoh was angry with his 2 officers, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.
Pharaoh put them in the prison of the captain of the guard, the same place where Joseph was held.
The captain of the guard put Joseph in charge of them, and Joseph took care of them. They stayed in prison for some time.
One night the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were held in prison, each had a dream. Each dream had its own meaning.
In the morning Joseph came to them and saw that they were upset.
Joseph asked Pharaoh's officers who were in prison with him: Why do you look so sad today?
They answered: We each had a dream, and no one can tell us what the dreams mean. Joseph said: Does God not give the meaning of dreams? Please tell me your dreams.
The chief cupbearer told Joseph his dream: In my dream I saw a vine in front of me.
The vine had 3 branches. It budded, and the blossoms came out. Then its clusters turned into ripe grapes.
Pharaoh's cup was in my hand. I took the grapes and squeezed them into Pharaoh's cup. Then I put the cup in Pharaoh's hand.
Joseph said to him: This is what your dream means. The 3 branches are 3 days.
In 3 days Pharaoh will remember you and give you your job back. You will put Pharaoh's cup in his hand, as you did before.
But when things go well for you, please remember me. Please be kind to me and tell Pharaoh about me. Then I can get out of this prison.
I was stolen from the land of the Hebrews. Even here I have done nothing wrong to be put in this prison.
The chief baker saw that Joseph had given a good meaning. The baker said to Joseph: I also had a dream. I had 3 baskets of white bread on my head.
The top basket had all kinds of baked food for Pharaoh. But birds were eating it out of the basket on my head.
Joseph answered: This is what your dream means. The 3 baskets are 3 days.
In 3 days Pharaoh will cut off your head and hang your body on a tree. The birds will eat your flesh.
On the 3rd day it was Pharaoh's birthday. Pharaoh gave a feast for all his servants. In front of them, Pharaoh brought out the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.
Pharaoh gave the chief cupbearer his job back. Again the cupbearer put the cup in Pharaoh's hand.
But Pharaoh hanged the chief baker, just as Joseph had said.
The chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph. He forgot him.

40.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Check: 'butler' is 'cupbearer' (explained in verse 1); 'lift up thine head' (verses 13, 19, 20) is rendered by its meaning in each verse; verse 16 'white baskets' is 'baskets of white bread'.

verses.text: After 2 full years, Pharaoh had a dream. In the dream Pharaoh was standing by the Nile River.
Out of the river came 7 cows. They were fat and healthy, and they ate grass by the river.
Then 7 other cows came up out of the river after them. They were ugly and thin. They stood beside the fat cows on the bank of the river.
The ugly, thin cows ate the 7 fat cows. Then Pharaoh woke up.
Pharaoh fell asleep again and had a 2nd dream. He saw 7 heads of grain growing on one stalk. They were full and good.
Then 7 other heads of grain grew up after them. They were thin and dried up by the east wind.
The thin heads of grain swallowed the 7 full, good heads. Pharaoh woke up and knew it was a dream.
In the morning Pharaoh was troubled. He sent for all the magicians and wise men of Egypt. Pharaoh told them his dreams, but no one could tell him what the dreams meant.
Then the chief cupbearer spoke to Pharaoh. He said: Today I remember my own wrongs.
Pharaoh was angry with his servants. He put me and the chief baker in the prison of the captain of the guard.
We each had a dream on the same night. Each dream had its own meaning.
A young Hebrew man was there with us. He was a servant of the captain of the guard. We told him our dreams, and he told us what each dream meant.
It happened just as he said. Pharaoh gave me my job back, and Pharaoh hanged the other man.
Pharaoh sent for Joseph, and the guards quickly brought him out of the prison. Joseph shaved and changed his clothes. Then Joseph came to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to Joseph: I had a dream, and no one can tell me what it means. I have heard that you can understand a dream and tell what it means.
Joseph answered Pharaoh: I cannot do it. But God will give Pharaoh a good answer.
Pharaoh said to Joseph: In my dream I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.
Out of the river came 7 cows. They were fat and healthy, and they ate grass by the river.
Then 7 other cows came up after them. They were very ugly and thin. I have never seen such ugly cows in all the land of Egypt.
The thin, ugly cows ate the first 7 fat cows.
After they ate them, no one could tell that they had eaten them. The thin cows were still as ugly as before. Then I woke up.
In my other dream I saw 7 heads of grain growing on one stalk. They were full and good.
Then 7 other heads of grain grew up after them. They were dry, thin and dried up by the east wind.
The thin heads of grain swallowed the 7 good heads. I told this to the magicians, but none of them could tell me what it means.
Joseph said to Pharaoh: Both dreams of Pharaoh mean the same thing. God has shown Pharaoh what He is going to do.
The 7 good cows are 7 years. The 7 good heads of grain are 7 years. Both dreams mean the same thing.
The 7 thin, ugly cows that came up after them are 7 years. The 7 empty heads of grain dried up by the east wind are also 7 years. They will be 7 years of famine.
It is as I said to Pharaoh. God has shown Pharaoh what He is going to do.
There will be 7 years of great plenty in all the land of Egypt.
After them there will be 7 years of famine. The people will forget all the plenty in Egypt. The famine will destroy the land.
No one will remember the plenty in the land, because the famine that follows will be so terrible.
Pharaoh had the dream 2 times because God has decided this. God will do it soon.
Now let Pharaoh find a wise man who understands. Let Pharaoh put him in charge of the land of Egypt.
Let Pharaoh choose officers over the land. Let them take a fifth of the food of Egypt during the 7 years of plenty.
Let them gather all the food of these good years. Let them store the grain in the cities under Pharaoh's control and keep it there.
This food will be saved for the land during the 7 years of famine that will come to Egypt. Then the land will not be destroyed by the famine.
Pharaoh and all his servants thought this was a good plan.
Pharaoh said to his servants: Can we find another man like this, a man who has the Spirit of God in him?
Pharaoh said to Joseph: God has shown you all this. No one is as wise and understanding as you are.
You will be in charge of my house. All my people will obey your word. Only I, as king, will be greater than you.
Pharaoh said to Joseph: Look, I have put you in charge of all the land of Egypt.
Pharaoh took off his ring and put it on Joseph's finger. Pharaoh dressed Joseph in fine linen clothes and put a gold chain around his neck.
Pharaoh had Joseph ride in the chariot that was second to his own. The people called out in front of Joseph: Bow down. So Pharaoh put Joseph in charge of all the land of Egypt.
Pharaoh said to Joseph: I am Pharaoh. But without your word, no one in all the land of Egypt will lift his hand or foot.
Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath Paneah. Pharaoh also gave Joseph a wife named Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On. Joseph went out over all the land of Egypt.
Joseph was 30 years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. Joseph left Pharaoh and traveled through all the land of Egypt.
During the 7 years of plenty, the land produced more than enough.
Joseph gathered all the food of the 7 years of plenty in Egypt. He stored the food in the cities. In each city he stored the food from the fields around it.
Joseph stored up so much grain that it was like the sand of the sea. He stopped counting it, because it was too much to count.
Before the years of famine came, Joseph's wife Asenath had 2 sons. She was the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On.
Joseph named his first son Manasseh, which sounds like the word for Forget. Joseph said: God has made me forget all my trouble and all my father's house.
Joseph named his 2nd son Ephraim, which sounds like the words for Twice Fruitful. Joseph said: God has made me fruitful in the land where I suffered.
The 7 years of plenty in Egypt came to an end.
Then the 7 years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was famine in all the other lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was food.
When all the land of Egypt was hungry, the people cried to Pharaoh for food. Pharaoh told all the Egyptians: Go to Joseph, and do what he tells you.
The famine spread over all the land. Joseph opened all the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians. The famine was terrible in the land of Egypt.
People from all the countries came to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph, because the famine was terrible in all the world.

verses.text: People told Jacob that there was wheat in Egypt and Jacob asked his sons: Why are you sitting and just looking at each other?
The people told me that there is wheat in Egypt. My sons, you must go there and buy wheat for us so that we can have food to eat and not die from hunger.
Then 10 of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy corn.
Jacob did not send Benjamin. (Benjamin was Joseph's only full brother.) Jacob was afraid that something bad might happen to Benjamin.
So Israel's (also called Jacob) sons went with other people of Canaan to buy corn in Egypt, because there was a famine in the land of Canaan.
Joseph was the ruler of the land of Egypt, and Joseph sold the corn to the people. When Joseph's brothers came to Joseph, the brothers bowed before Joseph.

Joseph saw his brothers and recognized them, but Joseph pretended not to know the brothers. Joseph spoke harshly to the brothers and asked: Where do you come from? The brothers said: We come from Canaan. We have come to buy food.
Joseph knew that they were his brothers, but they did not know that he was Joseph.
Joseph remembered the dreams Joseph had dreamed about the brothers and said to the brothers: You are spies. You have come to see how you can attack our land.
The brothers said to Joseph: No, we have come to buy food.
We are all sons from one father. We are honest. We are not spies.
But Joseph said to the brothers: No, you have come to see how you can attack our land.
The brothers said: We were 12 brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan. Our youngest brother is still with our father, and our other brother is dead.
Joseph said to the brothers: It is like I told you. You are spies.
Joseph said, I will test you and see if what you are saying is true. You will not leave here until your youngest brother also comes here, as sure as Pharaoh lives.
One of you must go and get your brother, but the others will stay here in prison. Then I will find out if you are telling the truth or not. You are spies, as sure as Pharaoh lives.
Joseph put all the brothers in prison for 3 days.
On the 3rd day Joseph said to the brothers: I fear God. If you do what I say, I will not kill you.
If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in prison. The other brothers can go and take wheat to your hungry people at home.
Joseph said, You must then bring your youngest brother to me. Then I will believe you, and you will not die. The brothers said: Yes, we will do what you say.

The brothers said to each other: We are guilty because we did something very bad to our brother. We saw that Joseph was afraid, and Joseph begged us to help him, but we did not listen. That is why we have these problems.
Reuben said to his brothers: I told you not to do it to the child, but you did not want to listen. It is our fault that Joseph is dead.
The brothers did not realize that Joseph understood everything that they said to each other, because when the brothers talked to Joseph, someone interpreted it for Joseph.
Joseph went out and cried. Then Joseph came back and talked to the brothers. Then Joseph tied up Simeon in front of the brothers.

Joseph told the servants to fill the bags with grain. The brothers had given money for the corn, but Joseph did not keep the money. Joseph had their money put into their bags of corn. Then Joseph gave the brothers what they would need for their trip back home.
Joseph's brothers put the corn on their donkeys and they went back home.
At the lodging place, as one of Joseph's brothers opened his sack to feed his donkey, the brother saw his money in the opening of his sack.
The brother said to the other brothers: They have put my money back. Here it is in my bag. The brothers became afraid. They asked each other: What has God done to us?
The brothers went back to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan. The brothers told Jacob about everything that had happened.
The brothers said: The man who is the ruler of the land was angry when he talked to us and he put us in prison. He said that we were spies in his land.
We told him that we were honest, and we were not spies.
We told him that we were 12 brothers, all sons of the same father, and that one brother was dead and the youngest brother was with our father in Canaan.
The ruler of the land said to us: I will find out if you are honest. One of your brothers must stay here with me. Go back and take food for your hungry people at home.
But you must bring your youngest brother to me, and then I will know that you are not spies but honest people. Then I will give your brother back and you may go to any place in our land.
Jacob's sons opened their bags to take out the food, and each brother saw that his money bag with his money was in his bag. Then the brothers and their father all became afraid and they trembled.
Their father Jacob said to them: You want to take away all of my children. Joseph is no more, and Simeon is no more, and you would take Benjamin from me. All these things are working against me
Reuben said to his father Jacob: Father, you may kill my 2 sons if I do not bring Benjamin back to you. Father, trust me. I will bring Benjamin back to you.

Jacob said: My son Benjamin will not go with you. Benjamin's brother is dead, and Benjamin is the only one left from that mother. If something bad happens to Benjamin on the way, I will be so sad that I will die, because I am an old man.

verses.text: The famine was very bad in that country.
The people ate all the grain they had brought from Egypt. When that grain was gone, Jacob said to his sons: Go to Egypt and buy some more grain for us to eat.
But Judah said to Jacob: The governor of that country warned us. He said: If you don't bring your brother back to me, I will refuse to talk to you.
If you send Benjamin with us, we will go down and buy grain.
But if you refuse to send Benjamin, we will not go. The man warned us to not come back without him.
Israel said: Why did you tell him you had another brother? Why did you do such a bad thing to me?

The brothers answered: The man asked lots of questions. The man wanted to know all about us and about our family. The man asked us: Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother at home? We only answered the man's questions. We didn't know the man would ask us to bring our brother to him!
Then Judah said to his father Israel: Let Benjamin go with me. I will take care of him. We have to go to Egypt to get food. If we don't go, we will all die, including our children.
I will make sure he is safe. I will be responsible for him. If I don't bring him back to you, you can blame me forever.
If you had let us go before, we could have already made two trips for food.

Then their father Israel said: If it is really true, take Benjamin with you. But take some gifts to the governor. Take some of the things we have been able to gather in our land. Take the governor some honey, pistachio nuts, almonds, spices, and myrrh.
Take twice as much money with you this time. Take the money that was given back to you after you paid last time. Maybe the governor made a mistake.
Take Benjamin and go back to the man.
I pray that God All-Powerful will make the man kind to you, so that the man will let your other brother and Benjamin come back with you. If I must lose my children, then I will lose them.
Joseph's brothers took the gifts and more money than they had the first time, and they took Benjamin with them. They went to Egypt, and they stood before Joseph.
When Joseph saw that Benjamin was with them, Joseph told the manager of his house: Bring these men to my house. Kill a cow and prepare food. They will eat with me at noon today
The man did what Joseph said, and he took Joseph's brothers to Joseph's house.

The brothers were afraid when the man took them to Joseph's house. Joseph's brothers said: It is because of the money that was in our bags the first time we came. They are bringing us here to catch us and put us in prison. We will be their slaves, and they will take our donkeys.
The brothers went to talk to the man who was the manager of Joseph's house.
The brothers said, Please, sir, we came here before to buy food.

When we came to the place where we wanted to sleep, we opened our bags and then we saw that each man's money was still in his bag. It was the money that we had paid for the corn. We have brought the money back.
We have also brought more money to buy food. We do not know who put our money back into our bags.

The manager of the house said: You must not be worried or afraid. Your God, and your father's God gave you the money in your bags. I have the money that you paid. Then the manager brought Simeon to the brothers.
The manager took the brothers to Joseph's house. The manager gave them water to wash their feet, and he gave their donkeys food
Joseph's brothers heard that they were going to eat with Joseph, so they worked until noon preparing their gifts for Joseph.
When Joseph came home, Joseph's brothers brought their gifts and then Joseph's brothers bowed down before Joseph.
Joseph asked his brothers how they were and Joseph also asked: How is your father who is so old that you told me about? Is he still alive?
Joseph's brothers answered: Our father is in good health. He is still alive. And again, Joseph's brothers bowed down before Joseph.

Then Joseph saw his brother Benjamin. (Benjamin and Joseph had the same mother.) Joseph said, Is this your youngest brother that you told me about? Then Joseph said to Benjamin, God bless you, my son!
Joseph went out of the room quickly because Joseph's heart was deeply touched over Benjamin. Joseph went into his bedroom to cry.
Joseph washed his face, and he came back. Joseph was calm again and said: Put the food on the table.

Joseph's servants seated Joseph at a table by himself. Joseph's brothers were at another table by themselves, and the Egyptians were at a table by themselves. The Egyptians believed that it was wrong for them to eat with Hebrews
Joseph's brothers were seated at a table facing Joseph. The brothers were looking at each other because, to their surprise, they had been seated in order, from the oldest to the youngest.

verses.text: Joseph told the manager of his house: Fill the men’s bags with wheat. Make it as full as they can carry and put each man’s money back into the top of his bag.
Joseph said: You must put my cup, the silver cup, in the bag of the youngest brother with his money for the corn. The manager did what Joseph told him.
Early the next morning, the brothers and their donkeys were sent back to their country.

After Joseph's brothers had left the city, Joseph said to the manager of his house, Go and follow the men. Stop them and say to them, we were good to you! So why have you been bad to us? Why did you steal my master's silver cup?
My master drinks from that cup, and he uses it to learn secret things. What you did was wrong!
The manager went out to the brothers and stopped them. The manager told them what Joseph had said
The brothers asked the manager of the house: Why does the governor say these things? We would never do a bad thing like that.
The brothers said: We brought back the money that we found in our bags before. We would never steal silver or gold from your master's house.
If you find the cup in one of our bags, you may kill that person and then we will all be your slaves.
The manager said: Yes, we will do as you say. But only the man in whose bag I find the cup will be my slave. All the other brothers may go.
Everyone put his bag on the ground quickly and opened it
The manager looked into the bags. The manager started looking in the bag of the oldest brother and stopped at the youngest brother, and then the manager found the cup in Benjamin's bag
The brothers tore their clothes because they were sad and upset. They put everything they had on their donkeys and went back to the city.
When Judah and his brothers came to Joseph's house, Joseph was still there. Judah and his brothers lay before Joseph with their faces to the ground.
Joseph asked the brothers: What have you done? You must know that a man like me can tell what will happen in the future.

Judah said to Joseph: Sir, what can we say to you? What can we say and how can we prove that we are innocent? God has shown that we are guilty. Sir, here we are now. We are your slaves, all of us, and the one who had your cup.
Joseph said: No, I would never do that. The man who had my cup will be my slave. The others may go back to your father.
Judah came to Joseph and said to Joseph: Please, sir, may I talk to you alone? Do not get angry with me. You are like Pharaoh.
Sir, when we were here the first time, you asked us if we had a father and a brother.

And we answered you, we have a father—he is an old man. And we have a younger brother. Our father loves him because he was born while our father was old. This youngest son's full brother is dead, so this youngest son is the only son left from that mother. Our father loves him very much
Sir, you told us to bring our youngest brother to you because you wanted to see him.
Sir, we told you: That young boy cannot come. He cannot leave his father. If his father loses him, his father will be so sad that he will die
But, sir, you told us if we did not bring our youngest brother with us, then we could not see you again.
We went to our father, and we told him what you said
One day our father told us that we would have to go and buy food,
But we said: We cannot go down unless our youngest brother is with us. We are not allowed to see the man's face unless our youngest brother is with us.
Our father told us: You know that I had only 2 children with this wife.
I let one son go away, and he was killed by a wild animal. And I haven't seen him since.
If you take this son away from me and something happens to him, then I, an old man, will be so sad that I will die.
Now, imagine what will happen when we go home to the father without our youngest brother—he is the most important thing in our father's life!
My father will die if he sees his son is not with us. Then it will be our fault if our father who is old dies because he is so sad.
I promised my father that I would look after his son and make sure that he was safe. I said if he did not go back to my father, then it would be my fault forever.
Sir, please let me stay here in my brother's place. Sir, I will be your slave, but please let the boy go back with his brothers.
I cannot go back to my father if the boy is not with me. I am very afraid of what would happen to my father.
